subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Safety, Self-Care, and Knowing When to Stop
essentialQuestion: What does taking care of myself look like when no one is telling me to?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of the stop rule as an adult habit rather than a class instruction in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe distinguishing training discomfort from warning pain using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply illness, injury, and graded return without a coach in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving sleep, fuel, and recovery as the base of any plan; correct it and explain why.
Connect when to see a clinician and how to describe a problem with building self-care into a plan instead of bolting it on and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Write the self-care and stop-rule protocol the learner will actually run as an adult, including the specific conditions under which they will stop, rest, or seek professional care.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: The protocol may be written, tabled, or described; a learner managing an ongoing condition builds it with guardian input around constraints they already have.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
